origin.description: Colour significant digits in the usual way, and send the other digits through the subtle numeric style.

arguments.name: negative, significant
arguments.text: Logical vectors the same length as x. They say which values are negative and which digits are significant.

origin.details: A significant digit is red when the value is negative and pillar.neg is true. An insignificant digit uses style_subtle_num.
origin.example:
style_num(
  c("123", "456"),
  negative = c(TRUE, FALSE)
)
style_num(
  c("123", "456"),
  negative = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  significant = c(FALSE, FALSE)
)

translation.description: The same choice. significant defaults to true for every element of x, and the result has the length of significant.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A string or a list of strings.

arguments.name: negative, significant
arguments.text: True, False, or None. None means the flag is missing. significant omitted means true for each element of x.

translation.details: With the default options the two examples print the same text, because an insignificant digit still follows style_subtle_num and that leaves a non-negative string unchanged. Set pillar.subtle_num to see the grey digits.
translation.value: A string, or a list of strings.
translation.example:
from pillar.styles import style_num

print(style_num(["123", "456"], negative=[True, False]))
print(style_num(["123", "456"], negative=[True, False], significant=[False, False]))
